Split the conjunction into two independent standard results.

1. For the cyclotomic divisibility statement, use the prime above \(p\) generated by \(1-\zeta\). The key identification is
\[
\mathcal O_K/(1-\zeta)\cong \mathbf F_p,
\]
so the kernel of \(\mathbb Z\to\mathcal O_K/(1-\zeta)\) is exactly \(p\mathbb Z\). Hence \(1-\zeta\mid n\) precisely when \(p\mid n\). This can be organized via a library theorem describing the cyclotomic ideal \((1-\zeta)\), or via the two intermediate facts \(1-\zeta\mid p\) and \((1-\zeta)\mid n\Rightarrow p\mid n\).

2. For the Dirichlet \(L\)-function statement, invoke the closed-half-plane nonvanishing theorem:
\[
\Re(s)\ge 1 \implies L(s,\chi)\ne 0,
\]
apart from the principal-character singular case at \(s=1\). The hypothesis
\(\chi\ne 1\lor s\ne 1\) is exactly what excludes that exceptional pair. Internally, the analytic mechanism is the Euler product for \(\Re(s)>1\), together with the standard boundary-line nonvanishing argument at \(\Re(s)=1\).

Finally, combine these two supplied results with `And.intro`.
